issues.legal_issue: A proposed amendment to a written statement must be allowed in full when the proposed facts bear directly on comparative hardship, even if they also relate to a concluded finding on personal requirement.
material_facts: An eviction action was brought on the ground of the landlord’s personal requirement, and that finding had been affirmed.
The matter was remitted for reconsideration of comparative hardship between the landlord and tenants.

During the remand, the tenants sought to amend their written statement; the proposed paragraph was partly rejected because it was considered an attempt to reopen the concluded personal-requirement finding.
The proposed facts also bore directly on comparative hardship.
issues.conclusion: The amendment should have been allowed in full, and the appeal was allowed to that extent.
issues.legal_principle: Under Order 6, Rule 17 of the Code of Civil Procedure, a proposed amendment relevant to an issue being considered should not be rejected merely because it also relates to a previously concluded issue. Facts bearing on comparative hardship are relevant when a court must assess that hardship in deciding or moulding eviction relief. No earlier cases are cited.

predicates.eviction_proceeding: The case concerns a claim for eviction.
predicates.remanded_for_comparative_hardship: The matter was sent back for reconsideration of comparative hardship between the parties.
predicates.proposed_facts_bear_on_comparative_hards: The proposed amendment includes facts relevant to comparing the hardship the parties would suffer.

issues.definition: When an eviction matter is remanded to assess comparative hardship, proposed facts relevant to that assessment require the amendment to be allowed in full.
